lines.text: In C, two threads each add a million times. The total should be two million.
Without protection, the total fell short.
An increment reads the value, adds, and writes it back. Imagine the two threads reading ten and writing eleven: an update is lost. In C, this data race has undefined behavior.
The mutex lets one thread at a time enter this section.
The atomic increment makes the read, add, and write one indivisible operation, so this counter does not lose increments.
Without protection, eleven milliseconds, and wrong. With a mutex, ninety-two, and correct. With atomic, 21, and correct.
How does this work in other languages? Comment which language you would like to see in the next video.
